correctness.rationale: Reconstructed necessity by parity balance and the modular-three residue obstruction. Verified that all six templates are pairwise endpoint-disjoint, cover complete consecutive blocks, and yield their stated length triples. For b>=2 the E/F/C/D/A decomposition realizes all nonnegative a,b,c; for b=0 B/D/A covers every remaining feasible vector except all-length-three profiles treated by the step-three Hamiltonian cycle. The distinction between ordinary and cyclic lengths holds for n>=3. An independent bitmask recurrence exhaustively agrees for n=3..10, and constructed outputs pass all checks through n=60. The finite tests do not replace the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The new mathematical content is an all-multiplicity solution when distances one, two, and three all occur, beyond previously established coprime-only, two-distance, equal-multiplicity, and selected monotone-profile results. Direct searches of published mathematical records and primary literature produced no theorem with the same quantified support and exact modular exception. The claim retains a stated residual priority risk for incomplete indexing; nonmatching retrieval is not itself a proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Search and bibliographic coverage cannot rule out every unindexed preprint or unpublished construction for the same three distances.
The odd-seat prior article was accessible at abstract level only; its stated group order excludes direct coverage, but its techniques could have implications not inspected in full.
Some included b=0 and at-most-two-distance cases were already known and are not separately claimed as novel.

value.rationale: A complete support-three solution treats a genuinely new nonunit-distance regime of a published seating-couple conjecture, with explicit finite templates for every multiplicity profile and a sharp composite-order modulus-three failure. This gives a natural exact classification, not arbitrary sample cases or a routine numerical table; it exposes when the known parity necessity is sufficient and isolates its only failure for lengths <=3.
